title: The Base Model Is Dead — Varun Singh, Arcee AI
talk_summary: This is a pre-training research talk about how base-model data mixes are shifting from web text toward code, synthetic data, and post-training/agentic distributions, plus how RL compute now rivals supervised pre-training.

takeaways.technique: Train/tune on the deployment distribution (analogy only)
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue models should see the shape of downstream tasks (chat, agentic traces, long context) early, rather than only generic web text, so representations match deployment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: exposing the model to the distribution that it would see during post-training in RL and at a longer context

takeaways.what_they_do: They cite work showing a base model needs exposure to atomic skills it will compose during RL, then can extrapolate if the environment is hard enough.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the base model needs to have some exposure to like uh like the atomic skills that it would need to compose during RL
